HEAD OF CONTENT

Bevado is hiring a Head of Content with a strong focus on video content creation.

Location: New York City, NY (onsite, five days a week).

OpenAI’s Robotics team builds hardware and software for general-purpose robots. We work closely with AI researchers and use what we learn from testing on physical robots to guide the next design.

About the Role
We’re hiring an Engineering Manager to lead engineers working on firmware, low-level controls, and systems software for onboard compute. You’ll develop the people doing this work and shape the roadmap with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. You’ll stay close enough to the engineering to help the team make difficult calls, whether that means running one more experiment on the bench or deciding that a change is ready to ship.

In this role, you will:

- Hire and coach engineers, give them clear feedback, and help them grow. Give experienced engineers room to lead designs and create opportunities for others to take on technical ownership.

- Set priorities with technical leads and partners in hardware and research. Decide how to staff the work, communicate tradeoffs early, and resolve dependencies that could hold up a hardware milestone.

- Guide work on embedded systems, from board bring-up and device interfaces to actuator control. Invest in reusable systems software so other engineers can integrate hardware, command it, and understand how it responds.

- Set the bar for changes that ship to physical robots. Use design reviews, hardware-in-the-loop tests, and measurements of timing, tracking accuracy, and fault recovery to judge readiness.

- Bring the right people together when a problem crosses disciplines. If an actuator misses its target under load, help the team choose the measurement that will distinguish a controls problem from a firmware or mechanical one.

You might thrive in this role if you:

- Have managed a team that shipped and supported software on physical hardware. You can point to engineers you hired or coached who went on to lead significant work of their own.

- Bring depth in firmware, embedded operating systems, or real-time controls, and can reason across all three. Experience integrating custom hardware or off-the-shelf robotic platforms is valuable.

- Have taken a robotic or electromechanical system from prototype through repeated use. You know when a quick bench test will answer a design question and when reliability needs to be demonstrated under load.

- Have led work across teams with different priorities. You can make a clear decision as requirements change, explain it to partners, and give engineers the context and autonomy to carry it through.

Who we are

We're Redis. We built the product that runs the fast apps our world runs on. (If you checked the weather, used your credit card, or looked at your flight status online today, you’re welcome.) At Redis, you’ll work with the fastest, simplest technology in the business-whether you’re building it, telling its story, or selling it to our 10,000+ worldwide customers. We’re creating a faster world with simpler experiences. You in?

SENIOR AI RESEARCH ENGINEER

WHY WOULD YOU LOVE THIS JOB?

We're hiring a Senior AI Research Engineer in Vancouver to work on how agents learn from experience. You'll focus on two Iris products: Agent Memory and Agent Playbooks. Together they decide what an agent keeps from its past work and how that changes what it does next.

Most of the hard problems here are still open. When should an agent write something down? What happens when a user's preferences change, or two facts conflict? How does an agent turn a task it solved once into a skill it can reuse, and how does that skill improve each time it runs? Which questions in a support log deserve to become an FAQ? And how do you do any of this without blowing up latency or token cost?

This is a research role, and a highly applied one. You'll spend your time reading the literature, forming hypotheses, and running experiments that tell us what actually works. The research counts when it makes Memory and Playbooks better for our customers.

WHAT YOU'LL DO

- Drive the research agenda for agent memory and learning: read the literature, form hypotheses, and design the experiments that test them

- Reproduce promising papers against our baselines, and decide which ideas earn a place in the product

- Research extraction beyond facts: self-improving skills learned from agent runs, FAQs mined from conversations, and other reusable knowledge for Agent Playbooks

- Improve how memories get extracted, merged, updated, and expired

- Study retrieval quality, including hybrid lexical and vector search, re-ranking, query rewriting, and recall that accounts for time and entities

- Find efficiency gains with quality held constant: cheaper extraction models, smaller context payloads, caching, and fewer LLM calls per operation

- Own the eval methodology for Memory and Playbooks, from public benchmarks like LongMemEval and LoCoMo to evals built from customer traffic

- Work with customers on the cases where quality breaks, and turn them into research questions

- Partner with the Iris engineering team to carry results into production

- Publish your work. We support papers, talks, and open-source releases

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

In your first six months:

- The team trusts the eval suite enough to block a release on it

- Research results have led to changes in production

- Agent Memory scores higher on LongMemEval and our internal sets without losing efficiency

- Agent Playbooks has a working method for learning and refining skills from agent runs, measured on real customer tasks

- Cost per memory operation drops without a meaningful loss in quality

WHERE THIS ROLE SITS

You'd sit on the research side of the Iris team and work closely with engineering. Platform engineers own reliability and infrastructure, and product owns the roadmap. You own the research questions behind Memory and Playbooks: which ideas are worth pursuing, how we measure them, and when a result is strong enough to ship.

- A background in information retrieval

Package and Price:

• Design each offering as a module that combines with others into a larger comprehensive solution.

Take Offerings to Market:

• Map the customer journey and the strategic use cases we pursue based on differentiation.
